articleTitle: Plenary Speech
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Provides an abstract of the keynote presentation and may include a brief professional biography of the presenter. The complete presentation was not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Robotic System with Intel® Automatic In-Board Characterization for Customer Board Design Quality Check
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Intel ® Automatic In-Board Characterization (AIBC) is established for fast, robust, and accurate printed circuit board (PCB) characterization. It can provide comprehensive impedance analysis of thousands signals for the design quality check and PCB manufacture management. The comprehensive impedance and insertion loss can be efficiently analyzed for risk evaluation by comparing with reference platform. This approach can help designers not only verify PCB technologies, such as back drill impact, but also make the right decision based on trade off study between the performance and cost.

articleTitle: Parallelizing Time-Delay Recurrent Neural Network Modeling Technique on Multi-Core Architectures
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: A parallel time-delay recurrent neural network method for modeling transient behavior of circuits and components is presented in this paper. The training procedure of the conventional recurrent neural network (RNN) is very time-consuming, and, therefore, it was effectively parallelized for performing training on CPU and GPU multi-core processors. Modeling using this parallel RNN (PRNN) method not only results in faster evaluation of the created models compared to traditional circuit simulation tools but also excessively speedup the training process. The proposed method has been validated through transient modeling of TI's LM324 operational amplifier.

articleTitle: Integrating Parallel Computation Technique to State-Space Dynamic Neural Network Modeling of Optical Fiber
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: In this paper, the previously known state-space dynamic neural network has been formulated such that it can be suitable for parallel computation. Using the parallelization method makes the model training extremely faster. In addition, the final models created using this technique have much smaller evaluation times compared to conventional models present in traditional circuit simulation tools. Finally, the proposed method has been validated through transient modeling of 100KM optical fiber.

articleTitle: The effect of data distribution in Ensemble Learning Algorithms on WLCSP reliability Prediction
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: As the consumer market is growing faster and faster, the technology is changing with each passing day, and we are focusing much more on the reliability of electronic packaging. Electronic packaging is primarily used to protect the complex structure of IC components, which is of considerable importance in the semiconductor industry. We are working on assessing the reliability of electronic packaging using Accelerated Thermal Cycle Testing (ATCT). ATCT is an important test to evaluate the reliability of packaging. ATCT can judge the reliability of electronic packaging, but the experiment requires a many time and expense. It commonly applies the Finite Element Analysis (FEA) replace of experiments to efficiently decrease the testing time. Although FEA spends less time than ATCT, using FEA takes a lot of time building a model to obtain simulation results. We build models based on different parameter settings and apply thermal cycling loads on the models to get the reliability life of electronic packaging. However, multiple researchers may also get different simulation results. With the development of computer equipment, computing performance has high performance and with the booming development of artificial intelligence, this research applies machine learning methods. If we can use a validated Finite Element Model (FEM) data to generate a series of the data for Machine Learning (ML). It can immediately apply ML methods to judge the reliability of electronic packaging. It can save time to build models and avoids the mistake in simulation. Four algorithms are used in this study to evaluate the reliability of Wafer Level Chip Scale Packaging (WLCSP). These algorithms are Random Forest, Extremely Randomized Trees, Adaptive Boosting, Gradient Boosting. We verify our simulation results by comparing them to experimental results. When the simulation of the model is successfully verified, we will use the same modeling method to build a different database with multiple data volumes from FEM. To explore the influence of the distribution of different data volumes on these algorithms and find the algorithm with the most stable prediction performance and performance results.

articleTitle: Effects of Thermal Characteristics of Power Module on Electric Vehicle Inverter
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The thermal characteristics of power modules have a great impact on the performance of the inverter system in electric vehicles. The poor thermal characteristics of power modules will reduce the efficiency, power density, and reliability of the EV inverter. This paper studied the thermal characteristics of power modules under different power and thermal conditions and their influence on system performance in the EV inverter. The thermal resistances of Si IGBT and SiC power modules were measured by electrical method. The results showed the thermal resistance will be variated under several different input currents, cooling water flow rates, and inlet water temperatures. The thermal resistances of Si IGBT and SiC power modules were compared and discussed. We studied the structure-function to analyze thermal resistance in different material layers of the power module to find the heat transfer bottleneck in the Si IGBT and SiC power modules. Finally, by using the electro-thermal RC model coupled with the power loss model, the thermal effects on the inverter system were studied.

articleTitle: Quality Management and Analysis for the Power Circuit Design of Embedded Digital System
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This paper pay attention to the layout considerations of the switching power supply circuit board, the design techniques of heat dissipation for circuit board, and the method of reducing coupling interference. For reducing EMI noise with the most suitable layout considerations will be discussed in depth and the test results of the implemented circuit will be investigated and to analyze and compare their performance.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Techniques Implement Circuit board inspection in Smart Industrial
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This paper proposed deep learning techniques to implement circuit board inspection. Recently, machine learning, cognitive computing, and considerable progress have been progressed. For example, neural networks (NN), convolutional neural networks (CNN), recurrent neural networks (RNN) and long and short-term memory (LSTM), etc., have been widely used in image recognition and time series inference industrial internet of things field, in which image recognition tasks for computer vision has surpassed human vision. In this study, we used the TensorFlow tool to recognize the microcontroller package position that finds the correct location in a circuit board. It is an important indicator for outbound production.

articleTitle: Simulation and Measurement Work for 28GHz AiP Design of 5G Communication Application
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: In this paper, we present a patch antenna on a 4+2+4 substrate with a size of 13×13, and a thickness of 0.92 mm. There are 4 antennas in this package with same design. This stacked patch antenna provides −10dB impedance bandwidth covers 28GHz (26–31 GHz) for global 5G applications at mmWave frequencies. Within the bandwidth, the isolation between the ports is better than 20dB. The realized gain is higher than 5dBi at 28GHz, and the peak realized gain is about 5.3dBi for each antenna. In addition to the simulated data, it also contains the actual measurement results. All simulation data in this paper is analyzed by Ansys HFSS. And the most important measurement data is measured by the ASE E-LAB millimeter wave chamber. AiP substrates are produced through ASEE.

articleTitle: PSO-based Modified Convolution Neural Network on Fan-Out Panel Level Package Prediction
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Electronic packaging has become a critical technology due to market demand. Fan-Out Panel Level Packaging (FO-PLP) has become the industry's most popular packaging due to its large area and good use ratio. It is important to consider warpage issues during molding. Excessive warpage will make the next process impossible. Measuring the warpage of panel-level packages with different geometries has become one of the important tasks. Testing the warpage in an experiment way will take a lot of time. Many researchers use simulations instead of experiments to save time and cost. In this study, we use the Finite Element Method (FEM) instead of experiments. When simulating the Fan-out panel level package, we build a model for a variety of geometric shapes, and then we apply the boundary conditions and thermal loading. The equivalent CTE for the molding compound, which simplifies the complex material properties of the compound. In the end, we will measure the Z-displacement as the warpage value. Although the simulation takes less time than the experiment, FEM still requires a lot of calculation time and verification. With the improvement of computing equipment, artificial intelligence has become a popular method to estimate value and avoid human error. We use FEM to build warping datasets of different geometries for machine learning. Machine learning builds a trained model with the training data, and the trained model can estimate the value immediately. For machine learning, we choose Modified Convolution Neural Network as the learning algorithm. In Modified Convolution Neural Network, the filter will detect the edge of the warpage model. [1] The algorithm can select the important data points as the training data. Edge detection will reduce machine learning's overall calculation amount and ensure enhanced accuracy. An application of Particle Swarm Optimization [2] results in an improvement in learning performance and avoidance of local minima. The algorithm will use the wisdom of the group to help find the initial weight and bias to improve the accuracy of the estimation.

articleTitle: Establishment and Accuracy Assessment of Structural Equivalence of Fan-out Reconstitute Wafer for Asymmetric Warpage Prediction
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Asymmetric warping is an annoying phenomenon causing defects and reducing process yield of wafers and it must be prevented. Traditionally, full-scale 3D finite element simulations are usually used for addressing this concern. However, its highly computational cost makes this approach less effective and cannot provide analytic prediction to address the problem in a universal manner. Thus, a semi-analytical formulation is conducted in this work in responding the above-mentioned concerns. However, the semi-analytical formulation is only suitable for an ideal bi-layered structure for predicting the bifurcation state. In reality, a fan-out wafer is a highly heterogeneous structure. Therefore, it is important to perform structure and material equivalences for converting the original highly complex 3D structure into a bi-layered structure with equivalent uniform materials for conducting semi-analytical prediction. In this work, four material equivalence approaches are hired for finding the equivalent material properties. Their effectiveness would be evaluated by comparing the bifurcation temperature of their corresponding equivalent bi-layered structure and the original full 3D model. According to the comparison result, the material equivalence using energy method achieves the best result with the standard solution. Thus, it would be recommended for conducting future model simplification. Furthermore, structure equivalence is also taken into consideration for compensating the discrepancy in bending stiffness between the full and the simplified models for better warpage prediction. The simulation results indicated that the differences on bifurcation temperature and warpage between these two models can be reduced to 4.6 and 11 percentages with a computational cost reduction of 72 times. It is expected that such a cost-effective model would be very useful for packaging performance evaluation during early design stage.

articleTitle: Corner Analysis of Manufacturing Tolerances of 5G mmWave Antenna in Package/Module (AiP/ AiM)
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This paper discusses the impact of manufacturing tolerances on the performance of mm Wave (millimeter-wave) AiP through simulation. From the designed DOE (Stacked Patch size, Feed distance, p.p. and Core thickness) shows the important influence of component size. The stacked patch size is reduced by 25 µm (1%), the resonant frequencies are shifted to high frequencies by 0.3 GHz. The p.p./core thickness is reduced by 30 µm (11%/12%), the resonant resonances are moved to the high frequency 0.2 GHz. According to the DOE of each element on the mm Wave AiP, the impact of stacked patch size, p.p. and core thickness on AiP performance is more important and requires special attention. Understanding the key factors that affect component performance and ensure that the manufacturing process meets expectations. The deviations between design and measurement of the 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> and 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> resonant frequencies are both less than 0.1 GHz. The measurement results are in line with expectations.

articleTitle: Analysis and Optimization of a Multilayer Organic Substrate for mmWave Antenna in Package/Module Application
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This paper discusses the impact of manufacturing tolerances on the extracted material parameters for Millimeter-wave (mmWave) antenna-inion-package (AiP/AoP) through simulation. The T-resonator, difference length transmission lines (DLTL) method, and single patch antenna are used to extract the material characteristic of multi -layer substrate. Next, use stacking patch verify the extracted material parameters. Frequency shift is less than +/−100 MHz in the PP thickness +/−15um (+/−25%) process tolerance. Open-stub length variety of per 15um (1.02%) cause about 280MHz frequency shift. Core thickness variety of per 15um (6%) cause about 130MHz frequency shift. Patch size variety of per 25um (1%) cause about 240MHz frequency shift. From the simulated results can find out key point of affect which extracted material parameters. By the optical microscope (OM) measure the key points increase accuracy of extraction material parameters. Finally, this paper uses the extracted material Dk and OM measurement dimensions build simulation model in the ANSYS HFSS, the simulated S11 is close to measured results.

articleTitle: Development of a Low Cost and Raspberry-based Thermal Imaging System for Monitoring Human Body Temperature
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Since 2020, COVID-19 had caused about millions of deaths and huge economic losses in the world. Taiwan had a successful story of preventing COVID-19 invasion. Unfortunately, COVID-19 broke down the preventing a couple of months ago. In addition, Taiwan doesn't have enough the vaccines to stop the COVID-19 spreading. This event really let Taiwan people to live painfully and inconveniently every day. However, it is really needed a system assist Taiwan people to prevent from the COVID-19 attack. According to this need, we attempt to develop a thermal imaging which is capable of detecting the people with fever. The price of thermal imaging system is usually very high. Most of companies or organizations can't afford it instead of a cheap forehead gun. Although forehead gun can precisely measure human body temperature, its inconvenient usage increases employees' loading. This paper presents the development of the low cost thermal imaging system. The system consists of PureThermal Mini/FLIR Lepton 3.5, Raspberry cam, and Raspberry pi 4. The PureThermal Mini is a thermal module with smart I/O. It has a FLIR Lepton3.5 thermal imager. The thermal imager can provide the system a thermal image with the resolution 160×120. Currently, its price is around 15,000NTD. The resolution of the thermal image is quite low. In order to fit the need of the system, an image resize algorithm is applied to create a large size of thermal image for further application. About Raspberry Cam, it is a regular cam which can be directly installed on Raspberry Pi. Its resolution is up to 2592×1944 and its cost is about 1,500NTD. Its image can supply the system to deal with Artificial Intelligence process, such as human facial recognition. Raspberry Pi 4 is the core controller of system. It contains our developed Python program which is used to handle all of system processes. 3D printing is also applied to build the structure frames of the system. The cost of the developed system is less than 20,000NTD. It is capable of detecting more than two people simultaneously and automatically. With the assistance of the system, companies or organizations can efficiently protect their employees away from the attack of COVID-19.

articleTitle: Reliability Enhancement of Cu-Cu joints by Two-step Bonding Process
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This study shows the relationship between the interfacial recrystallization and grain growth in the bonded Cu joints with the reliability on thermal fatigue lifetime of Cu joints characterized by temperature cycling test (TCT). We adopted a 2-step bonding process to fabricate Cu-Cu joints using highly <111> oriented nanotwinned Cu (nt-Cu). The 2-step process includes a short-time bonding (300°C for 10 s) and a post-annealing step (300°C for 1 h). We studied the fracture modes induced by thermal fatigue and the increase of electrical resistance via the microstructural characterization. Finite element analysis (FEA) was performed to study the stress distribution caused by the large coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) mismatch between Cu joints and underfill during temperature cycling. We found that the electrical resistance of the post-annealed joints did not increase under thermal cycling while the samples without post-annealing showed 17% increase. Additionally, we found that the cracks caused by thermal fatigue can be further slowed down or avoided by triggering the interfacial recrystallization and grain growth. Thus, extremely small increases in electrical resistance were detected in the post-annealed samples.

articleTitle: Machine Vision Welding Defect Detection Based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Two defect detection algorithms are proposed in this paper because of the various types of defects in pole welding and the lack of obvious characteristics. Among them, the Halcon based defect detection algorithm can quickly and accurately detect most defect types; however, it cannot accurately distinguish between the bursting point and the welding penetration defects. Therefore, a defect detection algorithm based on Ray-Shooting is proposed. The Ray-Shooting model is a round core designed to extract pixel intensity characteristics around seed points. Firstly, based on the characteristics of the welding image, the OTSU algorithm and morphological operation were used to extract the welding area. Then, distance transformation is used to obtain the center point of the welding area and generate Ray-Shooting model at this point to extract features. Finally, the types of welding defects are classified based on the extracted features based on FPGA. Experiments show that this algorithm has high robustness. It can detect and classify the defects of pole pole pad, such as false welding, missed welding, burst point, welding penetration, etc. The accuracy rate of all test pictures is 100%.

articleTitle: Optimizing the Nano Wiring and KlettSintering parameters for low-temperature die to DCB attach of power electronic chips
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: KlettWelding-Tape is a sintering foil which can be used for die attach to replace conventional soldering techniques. As sown in Figure 2, it consists of a pure copper sheet which is on both sides covered with electrochemical deposited NanoWires [1]–[3]. The standard design is a 20 µm copper core with a 45 µm NanoWiring made of copper with a diameter of 1000 nm. The Nanowire coating enables a sintering process to another surface. As shown in Figure 1, the KlettWelding Tape is placed between the joining partners. Subsequently the partners are heated and pressed together resulting in a strong and pure copper interconnect.

articleTitle: The Effect of Viscoelastic Behavior on the Debonding of Underfill-Silicon Interface
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The driving force of the silicon-underfill interface delamination was evaluated with the consideration of the underfill viscoelastic behavior. The viscoelastic constitutive behavior of the underfill was first characterized under quasi-static loading conditions at various temperatures. It was shown that the underfill exhibits an obvious viscoelastic response at temperatures in typical packaging process and reliability test conditions. A generalized Maxwell model was adopted to describe the thermoviscoelastic behavior. A finite-element based numerical procedure was developed to evaluate the debonding growth at the interface. The evolutions of the fracture mechanics parameters including the strain energy release rate and the stress intensity factors were first calculated for a bimaterial interface crack in an infinite medium, and compared to analytical solution to validate the accuracy of the numerical procedure. The model was then applied to investigate the effects of inelastic deformation of the underfill on the debonding characteristics of the underfill-silicon interface. The numerical procedure can be applied to enable a quick evaluation of the interconnect geometry and materials selection for package design and process development. It would also allow the development of design rules for extending the package-level interconnect technology to the regimes of higher I/O densities.

articleTitle: Hybrid bonding enhancement system for ultra-low signal loss PCB manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: In this work we introduce a new bonding enhancement system to promote the adhesion of dielectric on conductor surface. Moving away from a traditional bonding enhancement process which solely based on mechanical anchoring to more advanced hybrid bonding system which enhancing the chemical interaction between conductors and dielectrics. This chemical bonding enhancer step in the process is commonly known as adhesion promotor (AP). In this way, the surface roughness can be kept as minimum as possible, ensuring high speed transmittance of signals in electronics assembly whilst meeting industry standards for adhesion reliability. Combination of nanoscale cavities and adhesion promoter shows an excellent adhesion performance and an outstanding thermal reliability. Outperforming the performance of currently available bonding enhancement system in industry. Thanks to the minimum surface roughness of hybrid bonding enhancement system, the signal integrity performance at high frequency bandwidth is improved remarkably around 8–10 %. Showing hybrid system as the best solution for bonding enhancement of next generation PCB manufacturing where ultra-low signal loss performance is required.

articleTitle: Optimization of Epoxy Molding Compound for Cu wire HTRB Robustness
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The material optimization of epoxy molding compound (EMC) for Cu wire High Temperature Reverse Bias (HTRB) robustness in the absence of accelerated humidity environment is presented in this study. The selected test carrier was assembled with Cu wire ball bond interconnect and Al bond pad material where Cu-Al IMC was formed during wire bonding. Positive bias was applied on the bond pad of the selected device during HTRB testing. Initial reliability test results revealed HTRB failures after 768hrs and 1000hrs at junction temperatures of 175°C and 150°C, respectively. Through intensive failure analysis using multiple characterization techniques including surface, elemental and morphological analysis, the failure signature was identified as Cu-Al IMC degradation, and the failure mechanism on ionic mobility was proposed. Based on the failure signature and mechanism, the critical properties of the molding compound were identified as baseline for EMC material optimization. The change in EMC formulation and its impact on the desired properties to achieve low ionic mobility for better electrical stability was discussed in detailed study. Further investigation showed that the molding compound optimization improved Cu wire device reliability by eliminating the occurrence of the failure mode initially observed and extending the device HTRB capability to longer duration up to 2800hrs at high junction temperature of 175°C. The key findings from this EMC optimization study provide a reference for material selection criteria on similar Cu wire bonded devices with tightened reliability requirements.

articleTitle: Copper Foil Characterization for High Performance Stack-up Design
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: In recent 5G era, the development of artificial intelligence (AI) technology has brought the technology to move faster, and the increasing data speed of high-speed (HS) input/output (I/O) interfaces lead to a challenging design for high routing density and stack-up. For instance, PCI Express Gen5 is performing at 32 Gbps while it requires a small loss budget at 16 GHz. In today's server product system design, in order to meet the high performance, the layer count cannot be reduced and the overall thickness is about the same. Thinner dielectric thickness is another consideration to create extra layers for higher and better performance. However, it will lead to more conductor loss, especially at higher frequencies. In this paper, the focus was on the material selection and proper copper foil usage in the stack-up. We found the importance of copper foil type, which should be applied not only on the signal but also the reference ground layers. The simulation along with fundamental theories were applied to support the results.

articleTitle: Development and Validation of a Semi-Analytical Model for Predicting Asymmetric Warpage of Fan-Out Reconstituting Packaging
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Fan-out wafer level package (FOWLP) are widely used in advanced packaging technologies. In modeling or curing phases the reconstituted wafers may warp asymmetrically due to numerous thermal and mechanical loadings. Such excessive warpages further impose concerns in subsequent processing and the final yielding and reliability of products. Therefore, it is desirable to develop an efficient evaluation to correlate the bifurcation of asymmetric warping. In this paper, the semi-analytical model is proposed for providing onset temperature of bifurcation prediction. And the finite element simulation of full-scale model serving as the standard reference in the entire work. Consequently, comparing with finite element result and the semi-analytical model prediction with several equivalent strategies, the semi-analytical model with energy method shows highly consistent with the full-scale model in bifurcation temperature.

articleTitle: Cell Oxide TDDB (Time Dependent Dielectric Breakdown) in Saddle FinFET
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: We demonstrated an optimization procedure of cell oxide TDDB (time dependent dielectric breakdown) in saddle FinFET. In planar device, oxide time dependent dielectric breakdown is decided by oxide thickness, oxide quality of ISSG (in-situ steam generation), and growth condition. Compared to the planar transistor, the TDDB in saddle FinFET is decided by two parameters - oxide thickness uniformity and conformity in saddle FinFET recess gate bottom, the saddle FinFET shape. In this study of DRAM, the 4G (four giga) consumer grade cell oxide needs to pass 10 years t0.01% TDDB life time. In our work, the outstanding cell oxide t0.01 % TDDB life time in saddle FinFET was introduced. The pristine sample could sustain 7MV/cm oxide strength and over 10 years t0.01% TDDB life time of 80 K (eighty thousand) memory density, but failed (6.58 years) in 4G memory density. The optimized process of in-situ steam growth (ISSG) improves die-to-die thickness variation, providing better cell oxide breakdown time (MTTF) in the three voltage Weibull distribution, which passes 10 years t0.01% TDDB life time as 4G storage memory. The square shape saddle FinFET provides more uniform threshold voltage 3-sigma variation control and less body-effect than the round shape saddle FinFET. The square shape saddle FinFET provides over 500 years t0.01 % TDDB life time as 4G storage memory.

articleTitle: Next-Generation Dry Film Photoresist for Advanced IC Substrate Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The continuous demands of advanced electronics devices with increasing functionality and performances has driven the IC substrate industry to increase the density of interconnects and to develop new package substrates with different structures. In order to scale down of copper traces, the advance of photolithography including the development of high-resolution exposure machine and dry film photoresists (DFRs) is highly required. In this paper, we report our research efforts on the development of next-generation DFRs used in direct imaging (DI) exposure machines for advanced IC substrate applications. The DFR product was developed through adopting a hydrophobic binder with a novel binder component and an optimized photoinitiator package to enable excellent resolution, adhesion, and chemical resistance against acid cleaner prior to plating processes. The newly developed DFRs can achieve line and space (L/S) of 5/5um with 25um thickness under direct imaging (DI) exposure systems.

articleTitle: New Solder Paste Solution for FCCSP with Embedded Trace Substrate to Increase the Component Stand-off Height
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: For years the consumer electronic products with light and thin characteristics are requested from customers, especially the mobile and IoT application. Thinning of IC packaging has been a trend for product design. Coreless substrate technology - ETS (Embedded Trace Substrate) is one of the solutions. ETS substrate is eliminated the substrate core layer, and utilize build-up layer to interconnect the IC and the PCB board, that is a widely used solution in industry nowadays. However, the substrate traces are embedded into the build-up layer, one of the structure challenges is that the space of ETS between component and trace is tinier than normal substrate. For the MUF (Molded Underfill) structure, it has the EMC (Epoxy molding compound) non-filling completely risk to cause the void and solder extrusion after reflow process. Therefore, the EMC flowability improvement is one of the solutions to reduce the void risk. In this paper, the way to evaluate higher SOH (Stand-off Height) solder paste is provided. Through the solder paste material improvement by adding Ni (Nickel) ball powder with higher melting point property to effectively increase the rigid and SOH of solder paste. Based on the different Ni ball powder content 4.5%, 6.6% and 9%, the SOH can be improved from 11 um to 32um, 36um, and 42um, respectively. In addition, we have finished the PLR (Package Level Reliability) collection with temperature cycle test (TCT), unbiased highly accelerated stress test (uHAST) and high temperature storage life (HTSL) conditions. All of the SAT and cross-section results were passed without void issue between component and substrate space.

articleTitle: Testing Algorithm Parameter and Device Area Effect in HfO2 OX-RRAM
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: We demonstrated an optimization procedure of SET and RESET parameters in HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-based resistive random-access memory (OX-RRAM). The vertical layout for the OX-RRAM is TiN/ AlO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>/TiN (top electrode/top interfacial layer/insulator/bottom interfacial layer/bottom electrode). There are four parameters that could decide the four performances of OX -RRAM, which are compliance current, interval operation voltage, maximum interval voltage and device area. The OX-RRAM device performances are compared with resistance ratio (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RESET</inf>/R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SET</inf>) and endurance. From the power consumption, resistance ratio and resistance endurance, we suggested a methodology of interval voltage optimization instead of compliance current in our OX-RRAM. After optimization, interval voltage 0.125 volts, maximum interval 4.0 volts with 10×10µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> providing 2.2~2.4 resistance ratio (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RESET</inf>/R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SET</inf>) with over 200 cycles was applied. The 10×10µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> has higher resistance ratio (RRESET/R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sET</inf>) 2.2,_,2.4 with 200 cycle. However, 35×35 µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> could also sustain 255 cycles with 0.8~1.2 resistance ratio (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RESET</inf>/R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SET</inf>). The flexibility of device area could provide different resistance ratio and endurance combination, where no further voltage or current optimization is needed. The smaller area OX -RRAM could apply as “buffer” memory, which requires small device area with placement flexibility. The larger area OX-RRAM with longer endurance could apply as “storage” memory, which requires robust endurance under higher operating frequency.

articleTitle: Die-stacking Placement for Heterogeneous integration Architecture
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: It is noted that performance (speed), power consumption, cost, and form factor are the basic driving forces for 3D integration. The wide application of heterogeneous multi-chip architecture in high-performance computing clusters has aroused great interest. The multi-chip placement can influence the signal transmission behavior in a heterogeneous architecture. Inter-chip communication has remained a major design factor due to the diverse traffic requirements in heterogeneous multi-chip systems. In general, to exploit the capabilities of a heterogeneous multi-chip architecture without I/O bottlenecks, dense vertical connections in stacked chips become of increasing importance in modern semiconductor technology. Consider a heterogeneous multi-chip architecture with a dense vertical connection system that gains a performance per energy benefit from fast state migration between these chips. Due to intra-chip floorplan constraints, it would not always be feasible to place communicating structures next to each other. To achieve higher bandwidth, the vertical connections operating at very high link rates become a necessity on-package. These certainly introduce potential signal integrity problems that need to be dealt with adequately. In this paper, interference communication between side differential multichip placement is analyzed through directional wireless links. The proposed inter-chip wireless interconnection is evaluated based on HFSS simulation modeling with multiple chips on a system. Various placement results are compared to demonstrate the inference of the inter-chip interconnection in a heterogeneous multi-chip architecture for exploring the signal transmission quality in an application.

articleTitle: Suitable for 2.45GHz and 5G compact dipole rotating antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: A rectangular flat printed dipole antenna with a small volume and area. It has the advantages of easy manufacturing and low cost when printing circuits. It can be separated from oscillators, amplifiers, variable attenuators, modulators, and filters. Phase shifter and other modules. Because this antenna does not require a lot of space, it is easy to install in the package structure cover. This antenna has practical value for teaching and can be used as a good subject for learning. It can include Bluetooth, ISM, and 5G has the opportunity to be used in future small products that can be connected to 5G antennas.

articleTitle: Plasma Treatment for Robust Interface Adhesion of Wafer Level Packaging
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Wafer level chip scale packaging (WLCSP) has numerical advantages, such as smaller form factor, high electrical performance, and lower manufacturing cost. And the flip chip package need plating bump as the interconnection to substrate or lead-frame. In order to re-route the electrical signal or facilitate a balanced metal bumps, the additional metal redistribution (RDL) layer would be necessary. The redistribution layer technologies require polymer/re-passivation as insulator to serve the rerouting purpose. Hence, the adhesion between metal and polymer/re-passivation or polymer/re-passivation and polymer/re-passivation will be a critical issue, which will impact to the package reliability performance. This paper illustrates the methodology to improve adhesion at the interface with specific index of metal or re-passivation bump shear. Two different main atmospheric plasma of surface treatment, nitrogen atmospheric and oxygen atmospheric were investigated from the point of view of adhesion for polyimide-on-polyimide and polyimide-on-plated Cu. Also, the general high temp polyimide and low temp polyimide present different surface morphology with variance adhesion performance under plasma surface treatment. By applying the mechanical shear force as the representation of adhesion, it will be easier to judge the interface bonding energy. The result indicate that surface plasma treatment is the recommended process for enhancing interface adhesion, and different atmospheric should apply for different pattern design based on the ratio of Cu to polyimide.

articleTitle: Novel Electrolytic Plating Solution for RDL in Advanced Packaging Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: With the emerging development of high-tech applications such as consumer electronics, 5G, artificial intelligence, and internet of vehicles, the need for IC chips featuring higher functionality, performance, and reliability but smaller volume is pushing close to the limit of Moore's law. To keep extending the Moore's law, besides development of novel nano technology for transistors, technology in advanced packaging in 2.5D and 3D are evolving rapidly. Introduction of redistribution layer (RDL) in an integrated fan-out (InFO) package allows better integration capability and lower cost. Copper electrolytic plating is one of the important steps in the fabrication of RDL process. RDL features blind vias with diameter smaller than 50 um and fine lines with pitch ranging from 50 um to 20 um or even smaller. Both via-filling capability and uniformity have remained two major key challenges for this application. Proprietary design of organic additives provides good via-filling performance down to 30 um vias without voids. To improve uniformity, simulation on COMSOL Multiphysics predicts difference of electric field distribution from ground surface to unit edge. Along with the simulation of mass-transfer mechanism in fine-line areas, novel selection of organic additives demonstrates differential adsorption along the electric field, creating differential suppression levels on different features, leading to achieve superior uniformity within unit with various pattern features. Besides extraordinary via filling and uniformity performance, a wide range of operating conditions and stable reliability offers key features for easy bath maintenance with this unconventional electrolytic plating solution. In summary, this paper demonstrates an innovative electroplating solution with superior uniformity for advanced RDL applications.

articleTitle: Using spectroscopic reflectometer with FFT method to measure film thickness on glass wafer of fan-out package
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Polyimide (PI) is one of the most important material of redistribution layer (RDL) process for advanced fan -out package and one of the key process is manufacture RDL on glass wafer. When the fan out advantage assembly package RDL layers increase, the each layer thickness need to be monitor for process control. Traditionally, the spectroscopic reflectometer is suitable for thickness measurement of thin film on silicon wafer due to the obviously refraction index difference between film and substrate. However, It is difficult to measure the film thickness which is coating on glass substrate due to the similar refraction index cause reflection signals form film and glass can not be distinguish. This paper mainly discuss the film thickness measurement on glass wafer by spectroscopic reflectometer with FFT(fast fourier transform) method. FFT method can transform signals from time domain to frequency domain and capture the highest amplitude reflection signal. This method can get accurate film thickness on glass wafer by fitting highest amplitude signal even the two refraction index of PI and glass substrate are similar. According to the verification results, it is proved that spectroscopic reflectometer with fast fourier transform is a good method to measure thin film thickness on glass wafer.

articleTitle: Polymer Direct Bonding Characterization in Wafer Level Packaging for 3D Integration
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Wafer-level polymer direct bonding technology suitable for 3D integration was conducted. Major parameters such as surface planarization, bonding temperature, and bonding strength are reviewed. According to atomic force microscope (AFM) inspection, as-cured PI films after the chemical mechanical polishing process, a flat bonding surface with Ra < 0.92 nm is obtained by planarization. The bonding temperature dependence (200°C, 250°C, 300°C, and 350°C) of the shear strength for PI/PI wafer-to-wafer bonding are explored. Wafer-level bonding temperature above the glass-transition temperature (around 260°C) of PI, the contact-area ratio of the PI surfaces achieves 100% contact by PI deformation. SAM observations have demonstrated a seamless PI interface, realizing with optimized bonding temperature 350°C. For the highest bonding temperature wafers, interfaces of bonded PI-to-PI areas are imaged by focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy (FIB/SEM), displaying the feasibility of these bonds. As the bonding temperature increase, the contact-area ratio is increased by PI deformation. Our shear tests and scanning acoustic microscopy (SAM) investigations suggest that the strongest PI-PI bonding is ascribed to a higher contact-area ratio. The bonding wafer exhibited a shear strength of 21.520 MPa with the highest bonding temperature, revealing the contacts successfully passed the shear tests standard MIL-STD-883, method 2019.9 (i.e., 5.938 MPa).

articleTitle: Low ESL Multi-terminal Capacitor Modeling
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Technologies being more and more expensive, being the first on market, it is important to be able to have a first time right solution to propose. In this context, simulation has to be performant, and near to the produced system. The ability to get good results depend essentially on good models of each part of the system. It was quite easy years ago when frequency domain and current consumption was not so high, because parasitic has low influence. Nowadays, each component behavior against frequency, voltage and temperature has to be known to get an equivalence between simulation and produced system. In this paper will be shown a way to model a highly-multi-terminal capacitor, to get all its usual characteristics as value, ESR (Equivalent Series Resistance) and ESL (Equivalent Series L - inductance), and also a suggested way to describe this type of capacitor.

articleTitle: Nitrogen Plasma Treatment on Titanium Dioxide Films Applied in Self-cleaning Glass
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This study reports the feasibility of nitrogen plasma post-annealing on titanium dioxide (TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) films applied in self-cleaning glass. Self-cleaning glass forms a photocatalytic reaction on the TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films coated on the glass during sunlight, making the glass hydrophilic, and using rainwater to remove dust away from the glass. Self-cleaning function are assessed by measuring the water contact angle on TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films. A low water contact angle means that the TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> surface has good hydrophilic properties. Previous study on TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films showed the oxygen vacancies in TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films are created during the nitrogen plasma treatment process to improve its surface hydrophilic. Our team has produced TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films which titanium films were thermally oxidized at different heating temperatures. It was hydrophilic after plasma annealing. However, thermal oxidation methods need more process steps to produce titanium oxide. Titanium films have to be coated first, followed by thermal oxidation process step. In this study, TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films were directly deposited by in-line sputtering with a TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> target. Three TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films with different thickness of 5, 15 and 50 nm were obtained. After that, the TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films were post-annealed in nitrogen plasma. Nitrogen plasma treatment contributes to increase of hydrophilic of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The structure, visible transmittance, contact angles and photoluminescence (PL) spectrum of the as-deposited and nitrogen plasma treatment TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films were compared. Experiment results indicate applied plasma treatment on TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films indeed influences the surface roughness and reducing water contact angle. The water contact angle of all as-deposited TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films is over than 50 degrees. The water contact angle reduces to less than 30 degrees after nitrogen plasma treatment. The films thickness of 5 nm corresponds to lesser contact angle of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films among all samples, where the films contact angle decreased from 51.81 (without plasma treatment) to 24.91 degrees. PL measurements were performed before and after nitrogen plasma treatment. PL spectrum shows that the PL intensity of the plasma treated TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is slightly decreased. Previous report implies that PL intensity decrease implies that the TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> surface has high photocatalytic activity. Improving hydrophilic property for TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films after nitrogen plasma treatment could be ascribed to 1. removal of organic contaminants; and 2. oxygen vacancies. The optimized sample thickness is 5nm for nitrogen plasma treatment. The water contact angle, and the average visible transmittance for nitrogen plasma treatments TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films (5nm sample) is 24.91 degrees, and 96.75%, respectively, which can be applied to self-cleaning glass. This paper contributes to industry of energy saving buildings and green materials.

articleTitle: The Impact of Carbonization on CAF in UV laser cutting prepreg
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: With the rapid development of consumer electronic products, a growing number of rigid flexible board is widely used, such as mobile phones, blue tooth headset, tablet PC. In the production of rigid flexible board, in order to form a good profile in transition zone, it is necessary to use non-flow PP. We need to cut off the corresponding PP in the soft area, which is called conform. In the stage of mass production, the operation mode of PP conform is punch, but in the sample stage, especially when customer need to repeat the production of sample, in order to save the cost of the mold, many companies will use UV laser machine to replace the mold. At present, the market has mature UV laser equipment, although UV laser is a “cold cutting”, there is still carbonization at the edge of the PP window, this paper aims the influence of carbonization of PP window on the CAF. Different types of PP and different laser equipment will lead to different degrees of carbonization. In this article, we mainly study the carbonization of nanosecond laser, picosecond laser and femtosecond laser in the cutting of different types of PP. The selected PP contains 1037 RC63, 1067 RC62 and 1078 RC68, and combined with the CAF test pattern, to explore the impact of carbonation on CAF.

articleTitle: Using ion chromatography for flux residue detection of integrated circuit package
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The flux is added to solder during the die bonding process in advanced packaging processes. The main function of flux is to remove oxide and to provide a clean solder surface in the integrated circuit package. Generally, specific organic acids are added to the flux to enhance the chemical activity, In order to prevent the flux residue, a cleaning procedure is performed to reduce the residue. However, if the organic acid cannot be completely removed by water cleaning after the heating and reflow process, it will corrode the copper surface and induce metal contact problems [1]. Therefore, it is very important to detect the amount of flux residue. This article introduce a method that uses ion chromatography to detect specific organic acids in flux and effectively detect flux residue.

articleTitle: 3D X-ray Microscope (XRM) Applied to Semiconductor Embedded in Substrate Defect Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This paper describes the non-destructive imaging using 3D X-ray microscopy (XRM) for Semiconductor Embedded in Substrate (SESUB) failure analysis. XRM is able to generate 3D views and 2D virtual images, such as via and layout of each layer of the circuit. [1] Three cases are explained how to identify and locate failures embedded deep inside the SEUB with 3D XRM, such as a trace broken, micro via (m-VIA) poor-opening within a SESUB package. [2]

articleTitle: Robotic Measurement System for High-speed PCB Electrical Characterization
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: As engineers keep abreast of the times for technology development, the specification requirements are more precise and rigid. In order to achieve higher data rate, lower loss material is widely adopted in PCB industry. In addition to impedance measurement for quality control, material loss is also a key factor affecting high-speed transmission. Therefore, measurement stability and repeatability are of paramount importance. The impedance measurement by Time-Domain Reflectometer (TDR) is widely used in the conventional PCB inspection method for high-speed application [1]. Besides the impedance monitor, the channel loss is more critical when the operation speed is going higher. Delta-L method is applied to measure PCB material loss property of the test coupon for the electrical requirements check [2]. How to characterize in-board channel accurately and efficiently is very challenging.

articleTitle: Enhancing Strength-Ductility of Cu Foils with Slanted Nanotwinned Microstructure
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Nanotwin (nt) strengthening is recently considered as the fifth strengthening mechanism in a certain material. It has been demonstrated that columnar nt-Cu films have excellent mechanical properties and great thermal stability. They can be fabricated by magnetron sputtering. Such a technique is costly because of its low deposition rate. In order to reduce manufacturing expenditure, rotary electroplating was adopted in this current study thanks to its simple and rapid deposition. We are able to produce a new microstructure of nanotwinned copper (nt-Cu) with slanted columnar grains. We found that the slanted columnar microstructure of nt-Cu is attributed to the enhanced mechanical properties. We fabricated the nt-Cu foils using rotary electrodeposition with various current densities and annealed them at some elevated temperatures. The results show that the slanted columnar nt-Cu foils have greater tensile strength and ductility than that of straight columnar counterparts. We suspect that the incline of slant degree leads to the activation of multiple dislocation slip systems. The strengthening effect of slanted grains contributes to the enhanced tensile strength and ductility of the nt-Cu foils, accordingly. As the current density and additive concentration increase, the slant degree between columnar grains and electroplating substrate is more inclined. The current method with high deposition rate is thus potential for mass production of high strength-ductility nt-Cu foils.

articleTitle: Research on Reliability of Non-Flow Prepreg Filling in Automotive R-F PCB
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: With the transformation and upgrading in automotive electronic products and the popularity of new energy vehicles, more and more PCBs are used in automotive electronic system. With the advantages of being lighter, flexible, small, and of multiple functions, more and more rigid-flex board are used in vehicle electronic products. Non-flow PP is an essential material in the production process of rigid flexible board. The use of non - flow PP is to avoid the resin flow to the flexible area. Low flowing is the biggest advantage of the non-flow PP, meanwhile it is the biggest disadvantage. Because the resin flow is very low, it is easy to lead to the occurrence of measling in lamination process. Measling will cause serious reliability risk to the quality of rigid flexible board. Therefore, the application of non-flow PP in rigid flexible board is being concerned particularly by R-F PCB engineers. Due to the complexity of the stacking design of the vehicle R-F PCB, the higher requirements are put forward for the quality and reliability of the non-flow in the process of lamination. This study is aiming at non-flow PP reliability of vehicle R-F PCB, and lists the main factors which affect the reliability. In this article, we mainly study copper thickness, core thickness, non-flow PP of different resin flow, PP filling test pattern, to find how these factors affect the reliability.

articleTitle: Investigation and Optimization of Mold Flow Impact to Leadless SMD Package Delamination
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: An interesting phenomenon on the effect of mold flow to leadless SMD package delamination was observed in this study. Delamination on molded package interface was detected on the saw singulated units coming from different locations of the map molded strip. To further investigate the impact of mold flow and seek possible optimization, an experimental design with different molding parameter, sawing parameter and BOM material was proposed. C-SAM was used to measure the delamination level in different areas of the molding block. Mold flow effect was investigated by changing the mold transfer speed process parameter, samples coming from the mold gate and vent area examined under high magnification after cross-section revealed the filler distribution difference. Results showed that slower transfer speed was able to minimize the mold flow impact, improve fluidity, and mitigate uneven filler distribution within the molded strip. Meanwhile faster transfer speed resulted to migration of fillers towards the vent area. Mold flow impact on delamination during saw singulation process was also investigated by changing the cooling water speed parameter. Experimental results showed that the delamination on the gate and vent slightly improved with faster cooling water speed, and the delamination difference from gate to vent was more evident. Furthermore, the EMC and leadframe material properties were optimized to eliminate the stress difference during saw singulation process. The surface morphology and roughness of normal and rough leadframe was characterized by SEM and AFM. The adhesion of the EMC to the leadframe was characterized by button shear test. Generally, with the higher adhesion EMC, the delamination was reduced especially in the vent area where the delamination trend is less than gate, however in molding gate where the sawing stress is higher, the impact is relatively minimal. Moreover, using rough leadframe with stronger mold interlock, the sawing stress can be sustained, making the molded leadless package more robust against delamination. The result of this study reveals a very interesting correlation between mold flow and package delamination level in leadless SMD package, it creates a new perspective to semiconductor industry for material and process development.

articleTitle: Solder Void Improvement Beyond Process Flow
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: In current SiP (System in Package) products, some solder voids in BTC (Bottom terminal Component) solder joints are usually out of USI specification, and even cause bridge after additional reflows. The solder void reduction is increasingly important to improve soldering quality and yield. The most effective way to solve solder void issue is to use vacuum reflow oven in SMT (Surface mounted Technology). However, the price of vacuum reflow oven is at least four times that of common reflow oven. Therefore, it is necessary to develop a way that is more cost-effective. This study started from parameter modification without process change. No matter optimizing the reflow profile or increasing the stencil aperture, the number of solder voids did not decrease. Therefore, process change was considered in the second phase, aiming to get a good void improvement. After baking for 20 minutes before going through SMT reflow, the solvent in solder paste volatilized well and the void % was reduced by around 20%, which makes solder voids within USI specification. The incorporation of this method in HVM will lead to process flow change, since an additional common reflow oven is needed for prebaking before SMT reflow. Nevertheless, the cost saving can be at least 50% comparing with the vacuum reflow oven.

articleTitle: A Novel Lead-Free Low-Temperature Solder with Excellent Drop-Shock Re-sistance
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The 2017 International Electronics Manufacturing Initiative's (iNEMI) Board and Assembly Roadmap had forecast a 20% adoption rate of low-temperature solders (LTS) for board assembly by 2027. BiSn solders are the leading candidates in these studies. How-ever, the intrinsic brittleness of Bi phases renders poor drop shock performance, which restricts it from drop-critical applications. An In-containing Sn-rich solder paste- Durafuse™ LT, developed on basis of Durafuse™, a mixed solder powder technology-allows re-flow around 200°C and above, and shows excellent drop-shock per-formance. The primary In-containing powder in Durafuse™ LT will melt first around 118°C to spread and wet. The additive Sn-rich pow-der will dissolve into the molten solder during reflow. After reflow, the solder joint exhibits a remelting temperature around 189°C. The drop shock failure of Durafuse™ LT joints reflowed at 200°C peak temperature is about two-orders-of-magnitudes higher than that of the BiSnAg eutectic solder. By optimizing the reflow profile, the drop shock performance of Durafuse™ LT is even superior to SAC305. Thermal cycling tests (-40 to 125°C, 10min dwelling) on BGA192 and chip resistors demonstrated the dependence of the char-acteristic life on the reflow profiles. A plateau-type profile is pre-ferred for excellent drop shock resistance and acceptable reliability performance. The success of Durafuse™ LT in mobile applications encourages ongoing work on second generation pastes, which will reflow at 190°C without sacrificing drop shock and TCT performances.

articleTitle: Upon Human's Unknown, Can AI Help to Address Uncertainty? A Practice on Package Substrate AOI Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: To recognize defects produced in manufacturing (MFG) process becomes a daily in-line and in-time challenge in today's semiconductor industry. This paper presents an AI-assisted defect inspection method for substrates, which are widely used in packaged IC products. With the help of Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) equipment and the adoption of Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Neural Network (DNN) technologies, manual efforts in substrate defect examination have significantly been reduced, and yet it is still insufficient for the high standard required by automatic defect classification task. One big challenge is that while MFG in-process conditions change, the defect variation also occurs. The defect variances may include some uncertain scenarios, such as compound of multiple known defects, or even out-of-domain (OOD), i.e., unknown defect. A question is then raised: can we build an AI model which has capability to address uncertainty just like human reaction when facing unsure situations? In this paper, we introduce a new ML technology AL-VAE which integrates Active Learning (AL) and Variational Autoencoder (VAE) techniques to enhance our field-deployed AOI defect detection flow. The AL can address the uncertainty and filter out the ambiguity, accelerate training convergence, and minimize the training dataset to reduce labeling efforts. The VAE aims at learning deep latent-variable distribution of image, which can reproduce the similar image's feature multiple times from latent space. Aggregating the reproduced samples can significantly increase the uncertainty information, especially for the unknown defects. To demonstrate the advantage of our ML method, the public MS COCO dataset and our MFG substrate-defect dataset are evaluated. The results indicate that our method selects around 50% samples from original training dataset, and the overall accuracy is still kept at the same level. In addition, the uncertainty information aggregating samples reproduced from VAE shows that our model can recognize the difference between trained classes and untrained scenarios. Our technology enhances the field-deployed AI-assisted defect inspection flow with human-like intelligence which can significantly narrows the gap between AI computing and human understanding.

articleTitle: High-Power Wireless Module Implement in Industrial Internet of Things Field
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This paper presented a high-power wireless module in the industrial internet of things field. The industrial internet of things field discussed wireless signal quality which has been a research topic. In the factory environment, many different interferences affect the wireless signal. Such as a Metal machine, 2.4G Wi-Fi Bluetooth network, and water wall. This paper proposed a high-power wireless module that used Sub-1G frequency and 20dbm RF power. In the experimental results are shown high power wireless module indifference test case that included through the wall, different buildings and high floor, in which have satisfactory performance.

articleTitle: Power Module Wire Bond Design for Reliability
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: As industrial energy conservation and the development of electric vehicles are getting more and more attention, power modules play a key role in energy conservation and carbon reduction. High efficiency and reliability become the major factors for power module design. This paper discuss the complex influence of bond wire, thermal, and current density in power module designs. It also includes building samples for power cycle test (PCT) experiments and compare with life time prediction model based on thermal mechanical finite element method (FEM).

articleTitle: RDL and Pillar Fabrication from a Versatile Copper Plating Process
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Advanced packaging suppliers are having two primary challenges during IC substrate fabrication. These challenges are not only in meeting the copper plating performance requirements but also in reducing manufacturing process costs. Copper plating processes must provide both high resolution and strict height uniformity within a unit/die (WIU) and within a wafer/panel. This is because the designs include features such as fine lines and pillars, whose top shape and coplanarity are critical to the product quality. To reduce manufacturing process costs, copper plating solution can be developed to plate multiple types of features in the same electrolyte, reducing the need for multiple plating tools. This flexibility allows fabricators to save on floor space, equipment and processing time. In this paper, an electroplating package, Systek ETS, is introduced to plate both RDL and pillars under different current densities in vertical continuous platers (VCP). The plating uniformity and coplanarity of both RDL fine lines and pillars were evaluated on a panel level. The Systek ETS package offered excellent coplanarity within a pattern unit for RDL plating. The variation in the plated height (or thickness) between fine lines of 5 µm widths and pads 50 µm widths respectively, was below 1.0 µm when using a current density of 1.5 ASD. The tops of the fine lines have defined, rectangular shapes and their resultant profile offers excellent conductivity. The same electrolyte package for pillar plating under higher current densities of around 5–10 ASD resulted in pillars with slightly domed profiles. These copper pillars had very good uniformity within unit and within panel. Physical properties of the plated copper deposit are essential for the reliability of the finished product. A few key physical properties are tensile strength, elongation %, and internal stress. Copper deposited with the electrolyte package had tensile strength above 40,000 psi, elongation % above 18%, and internal stress below 1.0 Kg/mm2. The physical properties of the deposited copper did not change considerably during the bath aging, showing that the package had a stable performance over bath life. The reliability of both pillars and RDL features were evaluated via solder dip at 288°C for 60 repetitions. The plated features did not show any crack or separation from the substrate.

articleTitle: Advanced Measurement Method for Thermal Interface Material Thickness of Flip Chip Package
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Flip-chip ball grid array (FC-BGA) packaging has become the mainstream of advanced packaging due to its high number of I/O pins. In order to achieve the effect of heat dissipation, the main method is to install a metal heat sink on an integrated circuit. The thermal interface material (TIM) will be filled between the chip and the metal heat sink as a heat conduction path and the bond line thickness (BLT) must be controlled to prevent affecting the heat dissipation effect. The traditional BLT measurement method is derived from multiple measurements by using a contact thickness gauge but the cumulative error is large. (The thickness after Heat sink attachment minuses the thickness before heat sink attachment). This article will introduce a non-contact measurement by using Scanning Acoustic Tomography (SAT). It bases on the sound wave transmission time of the TIM material to calculate the BLT thickness accurately.

articleTitle: Anti-Corrosion Capacity Validation for Anti-Sulfur Type Electronic Passive Components by Way of Various Flower-of-Sulfur (FoS) Methodologies
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Hardware reliability of Information Technology (IT) equipment can be easily affected by corrosive gases, moisture, contaminants and particulate matter. It can potentially cause electrical open failures due to sulfur corrosion (Ag<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S) on the inner electrode of electronic passive components. In order to improve the robustness against sulfur corrosion, many vendors adopted gold-based and silver-palladium-based inner electrode designs (noble metal) as well as other solutions, including passivation cover and reverse structure designs. New IT equipment applications, including Artificial Intelligence (AI), Big Data, 5G, Internet of Things (IoT) and Edge Computing in recent years has proliferated the need of passive electronic components and the industry is facing passive component shortage. Therefore, quality control is becoming more critical in reducing poor quality risk. Flowers of Sulfur (FoS) is a popular method to validate the anti-sulfur corrosion capability of electronic passive components. However, the condition of single corrosive gas (sulfur vapor) is not enough to represent the accelerated corrosion exposure in field environments. It has been stipulated that typical testing methods as outlined in ASTM B809 and EIA-977 may not be totally effective in driving Anti-Sulfur Resistor (ASR) failure occurrence at 105°C/750 hours (test to pass), or even longer duration. Despite testing at those conditions, end-customers have reported sulfur corrosion-related failures. Therefore, it is necessary to develop an effective accelerated method for anti-sulfur corrosion capacity validation for anti-sulfur type electronic passive components. In this paper, three conditions of FoS test were carried out to validate the anti-sulfur corrosion capability of ASR components. We introduced chlorine-gas as another acceleration factor, and benchmarked it against ASTM B809 and EIA-977 FoS tests. Several analytical methods were used in this work, including, high resolution 3D X-Ray Microscope (3D X-Ray), Cross section polisher, (CP), Plasma Focused Ion Beam, (PFIB), Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) and Energy-Dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX). Finally, we found that FoS with chlorine-gas condition is the most aggressive of all conditions.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave Receiver Of Radar And Lidar Detection With Deep Neural Network For Edge Electromobility
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This article proposed integrated millimeter wave receiver with hybrid beamforming of radar detection with deep learning, high performance, and low power dissipation. The microsystem also designs lidar detection to upgrade accuracy on embedded electromobility. The traditional pedestrian detection system (PDS) on embedded platform introduced as edge computing vision for advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS). The millimeter wave receiver promoted to reduce image computation with featured object and enhance throughput with parallel processing on deep convolutional layers of ARM Neon to comparison with produce MobileNet and training of others neural network.

articleTitle: Warpage Reduction on a Typical Fan-out Wafer Level Process by an Encircling Silicon Ring
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Due to temperature variation during the manufacturing process, and CTE (coefficient of thermal expansion) mismatch from different structure materials, thermal warpages were created on each fabrication step of a Fan-Out Wafer Level Packaging (FOWLP) process. In this study, a silicon ring encircles the dies above the temporary glass carrier was proposed for a typical FOWLP process. With the new ring, structure strength was increased during the manufacturing process so that the warpages were reduced. To verify process warpage reductions, finite element simulations were first performed through a commercialize software (ANSYS) for different structures designs, and effective material property equations for the redistribution layer (RDL) were employed to simplify the simulated structure. Taguchi method was next used to identify the optimal factorial combinations on design parameters. After obtaining warpages data in each of the FOWLP process step, the maximum warpage were found after glass carrier de-bonding. With the ring, warpage reductions were obtained in each of the manufacturing step, and maximum 86% of reduction was observed through Taguchi analyses for the warpage after glass de-bonding process. Since the ring was bonded to the glass carrier simultaneously with die bonding process, no additional process step is needed for the new methodology. Consequently, merit of the new encircling silicon ring has been verified.

articleTitle: Reliability Improvement for Next Generation SAP Electroless Copper Process
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Herein we demonstrate a well-controlled electroless copper deposition in semi-additive process fulfills good reliability on low-profile dielectric materials. Such metallization process sustains mechanical peel strength >0.4 Kgf/cm with substrate Ra <0.1 µm. Meanwhile, stable interconnect passes quick via-pull test without breakage at seeding layer. Further, metrology reveals the superior electroless Cu deposit throwing power of ≥90%. All these features guarantee processible and reliable interconnect solution dedicating to advance IC substrate applications.

articleTitle: Temperature Control and Improvement of Mocvd in 5G Chip Process Based on Quatre Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This paper adopts the conventional PID control which is widely used in industry as the basic research method and based on inherently safer design (ISD). Based on Quatre algorithm, the temperature control of 5G chip MOCVD, the principle of PID controller and two discrete PID control forms of position PID and incremental PID are studied. Taking the electric furnace as the research object, its object model is established. The PID control of the object is studied. The engineering tuning method of Z- N method, which is the most commonly used, is chosen as the comparative research object. When evaluating the control performance, several dynamic performance indexes and error performance indexes are studied, and the ITAE performance index is selected. Then, according to the characteristics of Quatre itself, a parallel communication strategy is proposed, and its performance is verified by comparing PSO and the original Quatre algorithm through function tests. The algorithm is introduced into PID controller to realize self-tuning based on PID control. The performance is verified by comparing Z-N tuning method with temperature control object simulation.

articleTitle: How the Type of Glass Fabric Affects PCB Insertion Loss in Different Resin System
publicationTitle: 2021 16th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: As the frequency of high-speed signal increases dramatically, accurate PCB trace modeling become more important. From the Dk/Df accuracy of the material itself to the roughness setting of the copper foil, it needs to be studied in depth to meet the actual situation above 16G+Hz. In this study, we discussed in depth the influence of different resin system and glass fabric on Dk and Df, and used simulation tool to modify the parameters to make the simulation results more in line with the real measurement. In addition, the research results are used to optimize the stackup of high-speed products to have the advantages of reducing board thickness, reducing crosstalk, and improving loss performance.
